method.purpose: Determine whether the flash score body is DRAM-bandwidth-bound, SM/compute-bound, or occupancy/latency-bound at the production d512 decode shape.
method.tool: Nsight Compute CLI under passwordless sudo (RmProfilingAdminOnly=1 requires admin counters)

tinygrad_probe.shape: d512 production tile: LANES=32, WARPS=4, TK=16, SW=1, MODE=2, LPER=16, nvalid=11, qhoist=0, grid=(48,8,1), block=(32,4,1)
tinygrad_probe.cold_profile_note: ncu profiled the harness warmup launch, which runs 64 internal iterations. DRAM/L2 byte totals are dominated by the first (cold) iteration; instruction and L1 totals were divided by 64 for per-pass values.

llama_probe.shape: d512 installed: grid=(1,4,32), block=(32,4,1), Hd=128, Hq=32, Hkv=8, Tc=512, fp16 K/V

conclusion.tinygrad_flash_binding: SM/compute-bound at ~60% pipe utilization with only ~19% occupancy
conclusion.llama_flash_binding: latency/occupancy-bound at ~7% SM utilization and ~8% occupancy
conclusion.wall_gap_cause_from_flash_counters: not DRAM traffic; the in-window flash_score exposure gap is a timeline exposure difference, not a bandwidth-limited body

observed: all ncu counter values and percentages in cold and warm profiles
kernel names, grid/block shapes, and compute capability
inferred: per-pass tinygrad instruction and L1 traffic by dividing the 64-iteration warmup launch
binding classification from sm__throughput, occupancy, and dram__throughput percentages
unmeasured: full-token per-family DRAM attribution for the 5.04 vs 4.70 GB/token ledger
production installed launch cold-start overhead and its interaction with surrounding graph traffic
